decoder_context: Fin d is the standard finite index type with values zero through d minus one. Its displayed sum ranges over every index exactly once.
Real.cos, Real.pi and casts from natural numbers and integers to reals have their standard meanings.

The divisor and quotient inside the conditional are integers. Divisibility has its standard integer meaning. An exponent of type Int on a real base is the standard integer power, including inverse powers at negative exponents.

reconstruction.text:
# Reconstructed theorem

For every natural number \(d\) satisfying \(2\le d\), and for every integer \(k\), define the real numbers
\[
\theta_i=\frac{(i+\tfrac12)\pi}{d},\qquad i=0,1,\ldots,d-1.
\]
Then the real finite sum satisfies
\[
\sum_{i=0}^{d-1}\cos(k\theta_i)
=
\begin{cases}
 d\,(-1)^{\,k/(2d)},& 2d\mid k,\\
 0,& 2d\nmid k.
\end{cases}
\]
Here divisibility and the quotient \(k/(2d)\) are taken in the integers. In the divisible case, the quotient is the unique integer \(m\) such that \(k=2dm\). The power \((-1)^m\) is a real integer power, including inverse powers when \(m<0\).

Equivalently, for each admissible \(d\), the value is \(d\) when \(k=4dn\) for an integer \(n\), is \(-d\) when \(k=2d(2n+1)\) for an integer \(n\), and is \(0\) for every other integer \(k\). These cases exhaust all integer values of \(k\).

## Quantifiers, objects, and domains

The quantifier order is: choose any \(d\in\mathbb N\); assume \(2\le d\); then choose any \(k\in\mathbb Z\). Within that scope, \(\theta\) is the uniquely specified function from \(\operatorname{Fin}(d)\) to \(\mathbb R\), determined by \(d\) alone. Each index has the natural value \(i\in\{0,\ldots,d-1\}\), and the sum includes each such index exactly once. Natural and integer quantities used in the angles and the real product on the right are cast to real numbers. The \(1/2\) in the angle is the real number one half, not integer division. The angle uses the standard real constant \(\pi\), and cosine is the standard real cosine.

The only hypothesis is \(d\in\mathbb N\) with \(d\ge2\). There is no restriction on the sign, parity, or size of \(k\). In particular, \(2d\) is a positive, nonzero integer, so the integer quotient in the divisible branch is exact, including for negative \(k\). No quotient is needed to describe the nondivisible branch.

## Zero, positive, and negative frequencies

At \(k=0\), the quotient is \(0\), the integer power is \((-1)^0=1\), and the asserted sum is \(d\).

For \(k>0\), if \(k=2dm\) with \(m>0\), the asserted sum is \(d\) for even \(m\) and \(-d\) for odd \(m\). Every positive \(k\) not divisible by \(2d\) has asserted sum \(0\).

For \(k<0\), if \(k=-2dn\) with \(n>0\), the integer exponent is \(-n\). The asserted sum is \(d\) for even \(n\) and \(-d\) for odd \(n\). Every negative \(k\) not divisible by \(2d\) has asserted sum \(0\). Thus the stated value at a negative integer is the same as at its positive opposite. All odd integers are in the zero-valued branch; an even integer is in a nonzero branch exactly when it is divisible by \(2d\).

## Scope and constants

The statement covers every integer \(k\) for each fixed natural dimension \(d\ge2\), with the same explicitly specified angles. It makes no assertion for \(d=0\) or \(d=1\), or for noninteger frequencies. There are no auxiliary parameters, unspecified constants, error terms, limiting statements, or further regularity assumptions. The amplitude is exactly the real cast of \(d\); the fixed numerical constants are \(0\), \(1\), \(2\), \(1/2\), \(-1\), and \(\pi\). The equivalent parity formulation introduces \(4\) only as \(2\cdot2\). This reconstruction states the mathematical content and its scope, without a proof or a claim about any source identity or source fidelity.

import Mathlib.Analysis.SpecialFunctions.Trigonometric.Complex
import Mathlib.Algebra.BigOperators.Fin
import Mathlib.Tactic.FieldSimp
import Mathlib.Tactic.Linarith

import Mathlib.Tactic.Ring

/-! Exact midpoint-grid cosine aliases, arXiv:2610.20492v1, Appendix C.3,
paragraph 3 / Ex139. Frequencies are arbitrary integers. The finite-grid
Gaussian expectation identification and closed moment sums are separate steps. -/

open scoped BigOperators

namespace AutoSamplingTheory.ExampleCases.GaussianComplexity.FixedSpectrumGridAlias

/-- The literal midpoint cosine grid vanishes off multiples of `2*d` and
has the signed alias value at every multiple, including negative frequencies. -/
theorem actual_midpoint_grid_cosine_alias {d : ℕ} (hd : 2 ≤ d) (k : ℤ) :
  let θ : Fin d → ℝ := fun i => ((i.val : ℝ) + 1 / 2) * Real.pi / (d : ℝ)
  (∑ i : Fin d, Real.cos ((k : ℝ) * θ i)) =
    (d : ℝ) * (if (2 * (d : ℤ)) ∣ k then
      (-1 : ℝ) ^ (k / (2 * (d : ℤ))) else 0) := by
  classical
  dsimp only
  have hd0 : (d : ℝ) ≠ 0 := by exact_mod_cast (show d ≠ 0 by omega)
  by_cases hk : (2 * (d : ℤ)) ∣ k
  · rw [if_pos hk]
    let q : ℤ := k / (2 * (d : ℤ))
    have hq : k = 2 * (d : ℤ) * q := (Int.mul_ediv_cancel' hk).symm
    have hqr : (k : ℝ) = 2 * (d : ℝ) * (q : ℝ) := by exact_mod_cast hq
    have hterm (i : Fin d) :
        Real.cos ((k : ℝ) * (((i.val : ℝ) + 1 / 2) * Real.pi / (d : ℝ))) =
          (-1 : ℝ) ^ q := by
      have hangle : (k : ℝ) * (((i.val : ℝ) + 1 / 2) * Real.pi / (d : ℝ)) =
          (q : ℝ) * Real.pi + ((q * (i.val : ℤ) : ℤ) : ℝ) * (2 * Real.pi) := by
        rw [hqr]
        push_cast
        field_simp
        ring
      rw [hangle, Real.cos_add_int_mul_two_pi, Real.cos_int_mul_pi]
    simp_rw [hterm]
    simp [q]
  · rw [if_neg hk, mul_zero]
    let a : ℝ := (k : ℝ) * Real.pi / (d : ℝ)
    have hsin : Real.sin (a / 2) ≠ 0 := by
      intro hz
      obtain ⟨m, hm⟩ := Real.sin_eq_zero_iff.mp hz
      have hm' : (m : ℝ) = (k : ℝ) / (2 * (d : ℝ)) := by
        apply mul_right_cancel₀ Real.pi_ne_zero
        calc
          (m : ℝ) * Real.pi = a / 2 := hm
          _ = ((k : ℝ) / (2 * (d : ℝ))) * Real.pi := by dsimp [a]; ring
      have hreal : (k : ℝ) = (2 * (d : ℝ)) * (m : ℝ) := by
        rw [hm']
        field_simp
      have hint : k = (2 * (d : ℤ)) * m := by exact_mod_cast hreal
      exact hk ⟨m, hint⟩
    have hgrid : (∑ i : Fin d,
        Real.cos ((k : ℝ) * (((i.val : ℝ) + 1 / 2) * Real.pi / (d : ℝ)))) =
        ∑ i ∈ Finset.range d, Real.cos (a * (i : ℝ) + a / 2) := by
      rw [← Fin.sum_univ_eq_sum_range]
      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
      intro i _
      congr 1
      dsimp [a]
      ring
    rw [hgrid]
    have hsum := Real.sin_mul_sum_cos d a (a / 2)
    have harg : (d : ℝ) * a / 2 = (k : ℝ) * Real.pi / 2 := by
      dsimp [a]
      field_simp
    have harg' : ((d : ℝ) - 1) * a / 2 + a / 2 = (k : ℝ) * Real.pi / 2 := by
      calc
        _ = (d : ℝ) * a / 2 := by ring
        _ = _ := harg
    rw [harg, harg'] at hsum
    have hzero : Real.sin ((k : ℝ) * Real.pi / 2) *
        Real.cos ((k : ℝ) * Real.pi / 2) = 0 := by
      have hdouble := Real.sin_two_mul ((k : ℝ) * Real.pi / 2)
      rw [show 2 * ((k : ℝ) * Real.pi / 2) = (k : ℝ) * Real.pi by ring,
        Real.sin_int_mul_pi] at hdouble
      linarith
    rw [hzero] at hsum
    exact (mul_eq_zero.mp hsum).resolve_left hsin

end AutoSamplingTheory.ExampleCases.GaussianComplexity.FixedSpectrumGridAlias

notation.text: The unnormalized sum on the actual d-point grid.

steps.title: Use the finite midpoint cosine sum
steps.text: Put x=kπ/(2d). The standard finite arithmetic-progression cosine identity gives a product formula. Its right side is half sin(kπ), hence zero for every integer k. This multiplication identity remains valid even when sin x vanishes.
steps.lean: hgrid transports Fin d to Finset.range d. Real.sin_mul_sum_cos, harg and harg' give the exact midpoint identity; Real.sin_two_mul and Real.sin_int_mul_pi produce hzero. No new finite-sum formula is copied into a public wrapper.

steps.title: Eliminate every nonalias frequency
steps.text: If sin x were zero, x would be an integer multiple of π, forcing k to be a multiple of 2d. Therefore sin x is nonzero in the nonalias case, and the product formula forces the grid sum to vanish.
steps.lean: hsin uses Real.sin_eq_zero_iff, Real.pi_ne_zero and casts to produce the forbidden integer divisibility witness. The zero-product elimination uses this internally proved nonzero fact.

steps.title: Evaluate the signed alias branch
steps.text: For k=2ad, use the zero-based grid index ℓ=i−1. Each angle is aπ+2aℓπ, so every cosine equals (−1)^a. Summing d identical terms gives the signed alias value. The exact integer quotient handles zero and negative a as well.
steps.lean: Int.mul_ediv_cancel' yields hq and its real cast. hangle, Real.cos_add_int_mul_two_pi and Real.cos_int_mul_pi evaluate each term; the finite constant sum gives d times the value.

steps.title: Consume C7 on the actual inverse grid
steps.text: For the private consumer only, fix real \(\kappa\ge2\) and a natural number \(n\) with \(1\le n<d\), using the same midpoint angles. Define the eigenvalues and radius by the displayed formulas. C7 supplies the reciprocal identity and absolute convergence at every actual grid point. Cosine weighting preserves summability, so the finite grid and infinite series can genuinely be exchanged.
steps.lean: The private actual_weighted_inverse_grid_alias_series calls canonical C7 for heq/habs. hsqrt and heigenlower produce positive square root and eigenvalues at least one. hmajor and hsgnorm explicitly produce weighted absolute summability; hs, hsg and hsumG give convergence. heigen normalizes the literal reciprocal eigenvalues, and Summable.tsum_finsetSum is the actual exchange. The public alias theorem itself has no κ or C7 premise.

steps.title: Keep only the two shifted alias modes
steps.text: The range 1≤n<d makes the constant grid sum zero by the new alias theorem. Product-to-sum cancels C7's factor two. Apply the same all-integer theorem at j−n and j+n; each inner grid contributes d times its alias coefficient. Summability of the resulting series is produced too. All differences are formed in integers before evaluation.
steps.lean: hcos materializes the new producer. hnnon and hzero remove the constant; hprod uses Real.two_mul_cos_mul_cos and both integer frequencies. hterm proves 2G_j=dF_j. Nonzero d transports summability to F, and hseries plus hexchange proves the equality. The compiled private consumer has precisely C7 and the new alias as public ASTIS parents, after expanding generated local proof auxiliaries.
